tagline.text: A 2,642 m peak of mossy forest and sea of clouds in Hungduan, Ifugao

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season (sea of clouds best in cool December–February)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: 2 days 1 night (a day hike is possible but extremely tiring)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱2,500–4,000 (per person, group trip from Manila, 2 days 1 night)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL), then overland to Banaue and Hungduan

children.text: Mt. Napulauan rises 2,642 m above sea level in Hungduan, Ifugao, and is the second-highest peak in the province. It is known as a punishing 2-day, 1-night climb through steep slopes and dense mossy forest to a summit camp with stars and a sea of clouds.
Mt. Napulauan (also spelled Napulawan) stands in the heart of the Cordillera in the municipality of Hungduan, Ifugao, at about

above sea level. It is the second-highest peak in Ifugao and is usually ranked around fifteenth in the whole country. The name is said to mean "whitened" in the Tuwali language of Ifugao, which seems to come from how often it is wrapped in cloud and fog. Stories also say that Japanese General Yamashita withdrew to these slopes near the end of World War II and set up his headquarters here.

It belongs to the central Cordillera mountain group, and on clear days people say you can see neighboring ridges such as Mt. Pulag from the top. The summit is in Ifugao, not Benguet, so registration and guide inquiries should be made on the Hungduan side.
The usual route climbs from Hungduan town (Poblacion), spends a night at a camp on the ridge, and descends the next day toward Hapao or Balentimol Falls. The elevation gain to the summit is about
, and the climb is rated 7 out of 9, a "major climb." Several sections require both hands and feet, so we recommend it for people with good fitness and proper preparation.

The rewards are real: a forest thickly carpeted in moss, a summit garden of bonsai-like bent trees, a sea of clouds spread below you at sunrise, and waterfalls on the way down. It suits travelers who want the rugged mountain side of Ifugao that Banaue rice terrace sightseeing alone cannot show.

The summit area is a garden-like flat of low bonsai-like trees and dwarf bamboo hugging the ground. It has room for about a dozen tents, and the moss-covered ground holds water well and feels soft underfoot.
From about
elevation, a forest thick with moss, ferns and twisted trees begins. It is long and wide and feels more mysterious than claustrophobic, but it is easy to get lost here, so stay close to your guide.

Dawn at the summit camp is the highlight of this mountain. On clear mornings the sun rises above clouds filling the valleys. Many days, true to the name, the mountain is whitened by fog, so you need some luck with the weather.
Climbing the Hungduan trail, you reach the first campsite at about
elevation. Water is nearby, so it is widely used for lunch and rests, and it becomes the first night's camp on a 3-day schedule.

Descending toward Balentimol from the summit, you first reach Mungkilat Falls and then the larger Balentimol Falls. Mossy forest and a narrow path along a drop are mixed together, which is thrilling but also the most slippery and dangerous route.

The Hapao descent looks down on the Hungduan rice terraces and the Bokiawan River from a grassy ridge and finally reaches the village along cement paths between paddies. The descent alone usually takes 8–9 hours.

items.title: 2 days 1 night: up via Hungduan, down via Balentimol
items.subtitle: Night bus from Manila plus summit camp

children.text: Take a night bus or a chartered van from Manila to Banaue. It takes about
9–10 hours
Arrive in Banaue, have breakfast, and move on to Hungduan by jeepney or chartered vehicle. Before entering Hungduan, register at the tourism information office in Bokiawan and pay the fee.
Start the climb up cement stairs at the Poblacion entrance in Hungduan. Hire a guide locally or arrange one in advance and climb together.
Arrive at Ny-o campsite and have lunch. It is a steep, exposed climb with strong sun, so bring a hat and plenty of water.
Leave Ny-o, pass the first water point and enter the real mossy-forest ascent. Ask your guide your position often so you are not fooled by the false summit.
Reach the summit camp, pitch your tent and have dinner. Night temperatures drop to
, so warm gear is essential.
Watch sunrise, have breakfast and get ready to descend. If it is clear, the sea of clouds unfolds.
Descend by the Balentimol trail. Pass Mungkilat Falls and Balentimol Falls in turn and reach the trailhead in the afternoon.
Wash up at the stream, return to Banaue by vehicle and take the night bus to Manila.
Times are only examples based on trip reports and group itineraries and vary greatly with weather and pace. Start in the morning at the latest so you reach the summit before sunset.
Travel from Banaue to Hungduan, register, hire a guide and set out in the afternoon. Climb about
3 hours
and camp at Ny-o campsite (
elevation).
After sunrise, have breakfast and set off to pass through the mossy forest (about
After lunch climb to the summit, pitch tents and wait for sunset and the stars. This schedule is the least rushed.
Prepare before dawn and descend toward Hapao. Look down on the rice terraces from the grassy ridge, reach Hapao village in the afternoon and return to Banaue in a vehicle you arranged to wait.
On the Hapao side the grass is sharp and deep ditches are hidden under it, so follow your guide and check each step.
Direct buses go only as far as Banaue. There is no direct bus to Hungduan.
Buses leave the Ohayami Trans terminal in Sampaloc, Manila, around
at night, with extra trips at
in peak season. The trip takes about
9 hours
and the fare in past reports was about ₱540. Reserve seats in advance.
If the Banaue buses are full, you can take a bus to Lagawe and transfer to a jeepney.
In the November–February peak season buses sell out early and schedules change, so check the latest announcements.
Small groups often charter a van from Manila and go straight to Hungduan.
Jeepneys run between Banaue and Hungduan, but reports say the first trip leaves around
noon and the last around
. Jeepneys from Hungduan back to Banaue reportedly run only between
and
in the morning, which makes planning difficult.

That is why many people charter a jeep or van. Past reports put a chartered jeep at about ₱2,000–4,000 and a tricycle at about ₱500 one way. The road is winding and landslide-prone, so choose an experienced driver.
If you descend to Hapao, arrange in advance a chartered vehicle from Hapao to Banaue.
Before entering Hungduan, register at the information office in Bokiawan and pay about ₱100 per person. Recent group tour packages include the registration and environmental fees.

Inquire in advance with the Hungduan tourism office or local contacts for a guide. According to reports, one guide usually covers up to 5 people at about ₱1,000 per day, and the total rises when the group is small or guides are short.
The Hungduan municipal email lguhungduanifugao@rocketmail.com is known as a contact. Addresses and contact methods can change, so please confirm.

For high Philippine mountains, the dry season from November to May is generally the safe choice. In the rainy season the trail is slippery, leeches are fierce and many days offer no view from the summit.
If you want sunrise and a sea of clouds, the clearer days of December–February and spring are best. In midwinter, however, summit nights drop to
with strong wind, and light clothing will not be enough.

Tent camping is the norm at the summit and at Ny-o campsite. The summit has a flat area for about a dozen tents, and there is reportedly water nearby. Bring your own tent, sleeping bag, mat and cooking gear; even group packages usually do not include gear.

Hungduan town has small stores where you can buy drinks and snacks. Still, it is safer to prepare fuel (butane gas) and food in Manila or Banaue. Some guides cook for you, so confirm the cost and scope beforehand. If you need a room, use homestays or guesthouses in Banaue or around Hungduan, and book through local contacts or the Hungduan travel page.
A 2-day, 1-night trip with a night at the summit is standard, and if you are not confident in your fitness, a 3-day trip that first sleeps at Ny-o campsite is easier.
A guide is practically mandatory. Trail ribbons in the mossy forest are sparse and it is easy to get lost.
Carry about
3 liters
of water and refill at water points on the way. Ask your guide where they are.
Prepare for leeches. Keep sleeves and trousers tucked, and bring alcohol or salt. Do not pull them off by force; make them drop with salt or alcohol.
Bring warm clothing (fleece, windbreaker, gloves, beanie), a raincoat and spare clothes. Getting wet is dangerous in the night cold.
Wear trekking shoes with good grip, and gloves help because many sections require grabbing with your hands.
Carry all your trash down. The mossy ground at the summit camp is fragile and easily damaged.
Leave slack in your schedule. In trip reports, the same course differed by several hours depending on pace.
Napulauan is one of the hardest hikes in the Philippines. Do not climb without registering and a guide, and postpone if rain is forecast.
There are many steep, slippery sections, and injuries have happened on the descent. Go down slowly.
The Balentimol descent has a narrow path with a drop on one side, and large rocks have fallen from the slope opposite the falls. Rest only in safe spots.
In thick fog it is easy to be separated from your group, and there are reports of hikers getting lost alone. Always walk together within sight.
The road between Banaue and Hungduan has frequent landslides and sharp bends. After heavy rain, check beforehand whether it is passable.
Many reports on trail details, fees and course openings are old. Before leaving, check the latest announcements from the Hungduan tourism office.
The UNESCO World Heritage rice terraces where the Hapao descent ends. A good place to look around the village after the climb.
Ifugao's signature sight, passed on the way to Hungduan, where viewpoints show the terraces at a glance.
Amphitheater-shaped rice terraces reached from Banaue by tricycle and a short trek.
The highest peak of the same Cordillera mountain group toward Benguet, famous for its sea of clouds and sunrise.
